subject: Staged uplift + co-term checklist for FathomRetail renewal
messages:
From: Nora Chen <nora.chen@fathomretail.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Usage spike & quick question on mid-term top-up

Hey Marissa,

Quick note — we saw a larger-than-expected uptick in inference calls during the promotional period in March (attached a trimmed export). We expect this elevated run-rate to persist for at least the next 6 months as we roll out personalization across two additional product lines.

What are our options for adding capacity mid-contract without paying full list price for a brand-new annual commit? We want to avoid re-architecting to reduce usage right now. Also, is there a way to align the added capacity so our renewal date (Oct 15) doesn't move out-of-sync?

Thanks,
Nora
Procurement Lead, Fathom Retail
Attachments: Fathom_usage_Q1.csv (CSV, 42KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Nora Chen <nora.chen@fathomretail.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage spike & quick question on mid-term top-up

Hi Nora —

Thanks for the export, that helps. Short answer: yes, we have a couple of common paths that keep your renewal date Oct 15 while adding capacity now. High-level options: 

- Staged uplift (recommended): Add a temporary capacity tranche for the remainder of the term that converts to a permanent annualized uplift on renewal. We can offer a one-time credit for the partial-term period to pro-rate the uplift cost.
- Top-up + co-term: Create a true mid-contract add-on that immediately increases capacity and then co-term the additional units to your existing Oct 15 renewal; this usually involves a small administrative pro-rate + a modest discount off the list uplift rate.
- Burst pool + overage hedge: Keep current commit and purchase short-term burst capacity with a higher per-token rate plus a usage cap. Good for uncertain spikes but less predictable economics.

I pulled a quick sketch with numbers and a recommended approach and looped in Ben for commercial math and Karthik for finance approvals. If you prefer, we can also surface a DocuSign order form and attach an amended Order Form that keeps your Oct 15 renewal.

Proposed next steps:
1) Ben to confirm the uplift tiers and discount band we can offer for a staged uplift.
2) Karthik to confirm accounting treatment and whether we need an invoice amendment or an addendum.
3) Quick alignment call (15 min) to lock in path and sign the order form.

Available windows today: 3:00–4:30pm PT.

Best,
Marissa
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Nora Chen <nora.chen@fathomretail.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage spike & quick question on mid-term top-up

Nora / team —

Thanks for the data. I ran a quick model. Two pragmatic proposals we can take to legal/finance: 

A) Staged uplift (preferred commercial): +30% capacity now, billed pro-rata for the remaining 6.5 months, then annualizes at renewal at a 10% discount to list for the additional committed units. We would apply a one-time credit equivalent to the pro-rated portion of the annual discount so you don't double-pay.

B) Mid-contract add-on with co-term: Add +30% immediately and co-term the new units to Oct 15. Price: 7% discount on the added units for the remainder of this term, and 5% thereafter when annualized. This minimizes paperwork but the customer pays a slightly higher mid-term rate.

If Fathom is comfortable with an order form amendment and a single DocuSign, A reduces your near-term cash outlay and gives better long-run unit economics. I attached a draft OrderForm_v2.pdf and a short checklist for what legal needs.

Let us know if you want to take option A — I can greenlight the 10% renewal discount pending Karthik's accounting check.

Thanks,
Ben
Sr. Account Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: OrderForm_v2.pdf (PDF, 210KB)
From: Nora Chen <nora.chen@fathomretail.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage spike & quick question on mid-term top-up

Thanks Ben — option A sounds reasonable. Two follow-ups from procurement: 
- Can you confirm the exact pro-rata credit math and show the invoice impact for April–Oct?
- Procurement will need a short statement of work (1 paragraph) that this is a capacity uplift only — no changes to data handling or SSO.

If you can send the invoice stub + the SOW paragraph, I can expedite sign-off on our side this week.

On availability, we can do 3:30pm PT today.

— Nora
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Nora Chen <nora.chen@fathomretail.io>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage spike & quick question on mid-term top-up

Ben/Marissa —

Confirmed: we can do Option A as stated. Quick notes for procurement/finance copy: 
- Pro-rata charge = (annual price of added units) * (remaining_days / 365).
- One-time credit = discount_pct * (pro-rated annualized cost) so customer only pays the net pro-rata after credit.
- Accounting: recognize revenue for the pro-rata portion when billed; remaining value will be recognized in the next fiscal year when annualized.

I attached a suggested 1-par SOW for legal. Laura, please take the attached SOW and OrderForm_v2 through standard redline (no commercial changes expected).

K
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Nora Chen <nora.chen@fathomretail.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Usage spike & quick question on mid-term top-up

Nora —

Attached is a one-par SOW for the uplift and a redline of the order form with the co-term language preserved. No changes to data processing or security commitments. If this looks good, sign here: https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/abc123-sign (DocuSign link).

On signatures: we can accept a signed PDF from procurement or a purchase order referencing the amended order form. Once countersigned, we'll schedule the capacity change for 24–48 hours.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
